raw_response:
*Thinking as this farmer...*

---

My name isn't important. I'm 51, I've been working this land since I was in my thirties, and my husband and two sons go out to work in the city now — so most of the farming falls to me and my daughter-in-law. We have 8 mu. It's not a lot, but it's ours and we know it well.

---

**Wheat first.** I always plant around Cold Dew — that's early October, around the 8th or 10th. That's what my mother did, that's what the village does. I buy seed from the village shop, the kind everyone here uses. I save a little from last year too, but mostly I buy fresh because saved seed doesn't germinate as reliably.

Before I till, I scatter two big bags of compound fertilizer across the whole 8 mu — that's the diammonium phosphate kind, the blue bag. I've done it this way for fifteen years. If I have a bit more money I'll add half a bag of potash, but if money is tight I skip it. The tillage I hire — the tractor man comes through the village in October and I pay him to plow and rotary-till for me. I can't do that myself.

In spring, around Qingming — that's early April — when the wheat starts shooting up, I go out early one morning and spread urea. Two bags across the 8 mu. If the wheat looks yellow and thin I might add a little more, maybe another half bag. If it's green and thick I leave it. I don't measure. I can see.

I irrigate three times for wheat. First time I irrigate right at planting if the soil is dry — I pump from the well and flood the furrows. Second time is in winter, late December, to protect the roots from freezing. Third time is in April, right before heading. I'd do a fourth time if the soil is very dry at grain filling, but pumping costs money — about 30 yuan each time — so I only do it if I have to.

For weeds I spray herbicide once in late October or early November, when the wheat is just a few centimeters tall. I buy the bottle at the shop and mix it myself. I've been doing this long enough that I know roughly how much to use for my field. Harvest is in early June — I hire the combine. It goes through in a few hours.

---

**Maize right after.** This part always stresses me. The combine finishes the wheat and within a week I need the maize in the ground or the season is too short. I hire the planting machine — it sows and applies fertilizer at the same time. I use hybrid seed, the kind from the seed shop. It costs more than wheat seed but the yield is much better, everyone in the village uses it now. Before planting I prepare two bags of compound fertilizer — the 45% kind — to go in with the planter.

Around when the maize is knee-high, late July, I topdress with urea again. Two bags across the 8 mu, scattered by hand. If the stalks look weak and pale I do a bit more.

Summer rain is usually okay for maize. I'll irrigate once if July is very dry, maybe twice if the grain is filling and there's been no rain. But usually the rain covers it.

Harvest is late September or early October, usually hired machines again. If my sons come back from the city at National Holiday we can help move the cobs.

---

**What I'm worried about this year:** One of my sons might not send money back as much this season, so I'm trying not to spend more than about 2,500 yuan on inputs total. I'll cut back on potash and skip the fourth wheat irrigation if the spring looks wet.
